issues.body: The validator still gates the prohibited-key lookup on `isinstance(flow, dict)`: `if isinstance(flow, dict) and "leases" in flow`. Consequently, a parseable top-level object such as `{"schema":"registry-observability/v1","flow":[{"leases":[{"label":"ab12cd340a5f9e71"}]}]}` returns no violations even though the public bytes contain the refused per-account array. The added `alien` self-test instead makes the entire document a list, which is caught by `if not isinstance(document, dict)` and does not exercise the round-3 finding. This also contradicts the updated README claim that the guard refuses the hiding shape.
issues.fix_hint: When `flow` is present, fail closed unless its value is an object; keep an absent `flow` accepted only if that is the intended schema. Add a literal fixture whose top-level document is an object and whose `flow` value is a non-object containing a nested `leases` array. Assert a specifically classified `validate()` refusal and add that case to the real CLI table with expected exit code 1, so both the nested-shape guard and its delivery path are tested.
issues.title: Non-object flow still bypasses the public-byte lease-row invariant

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-3 bypass remains. `_snapshot_violations` now refuses a non-object top-level document, but it still accepts an object whose present `flow` member is a list, string, null, or other non-object. The new alien-shape test exercises a top-level list rather than the reported nested `flow` seam, so it is green without closing the bypass. Because the same major finding remains at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
